title: Air India Wins Global Airline Strategy Award for Digital Leadership
excerpt: FlightGlobal recognises the Tata-owned carrier's sweeping technology transformation at a London ceremony ahead of the Farnborough Airshow, with CEO Campbell Wilson and digital chief Satya Ramaswamy accepting the honour.
body:
Air India has been recognised with the Airline Strategy Award for Digital Leadership by FlightGlobal, the UK-based aviation data and news platform. CEO and Managing Director Campbell Wilson and Chief Digital and Technology Officer Dr Satya Ramaswamy received the award at a ceremony organised in London by FlightGlobal in partnership with management consulting firm Korn Ferry on July 19.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wgqw0m2jNyU

The ceremony, held annually on the eve of the Farnborough Airshow, celebrates excellence across nine categories including executive leadership, ESG, and digital innovation. An independent panel of domain experts — comprising industry analysts, consultants, and former airline CEOs — selects the winners. Other honourees at the 2026 ceremony included Aegean Airlines chief Dimitris Gerogiannis, who won the Airline Business Award, along with Air Arabia, Alaska Air Group, Cathay Pacific, LATAM Airlines, Ryanair, Amazon Air, and DHL Airways.

From Near-Zero to 140 Systems

When the Tata Group reacquired Air India in January 2022, the airline's digital infrastructure was, by its own admission, skeletal. Staff relied on private Gmail accounts for official communication. Reservation systems were outdated. The carrier inherited what Dr Ramaswamy described as "a handful of systems."

Four years later, Air India operates more than 140 digital systems underpinning everything from booking and crew management to predictive maintenance and customer service. The airline bypassed legacy modernisation in favour of building cloud-native, AI-driven architectures from scratch — turning what it calls a structural weakness into a strategic advantage.

"Starting with a base of a handful of systems, we have laid down an extensive digital landscape with more than 140 systems in Air India after its return to the Tata Group."

— Dr Satya Ramaswamy, Chief Digital and Technology Officer, Air India

AI at the Core

Central to the transformation is AI.g, Air India's generative AI virtual assistant launched in May 2023. It has processed over 20 million customer inquiries, resolving 97% without human intervention, according to the airline. Call wait times dropped to roughly 10 seconds. Customer refunds now clear within a single day.

The airline currently deploys three categories of AI — predictive, generative, and agentic — across more than 100 internal initiatives, with over 30 agent-led workflows in development. Specialised tools include AI FlightPro, a companion app for pilots, and CE Plus, a management system for cabin supervisors. A partnership with Salesforce on its Agentforce platform is automating additional customer workflows.

The airline's mobile app, which features the AI.g assistant and a pioneering flight-status tracker that displays information about incoming aircraft, holds a 4.7 rating on Apple's iOS App Store in India — the highest for any Indian carrier.

Fleet and Connectivity Upgrades

The digital overhaul runs parallel to one of the largest fleet modernisation programmes in aviation history. Air India has ordered 570 new aircraft and is spending $400 million to retrofit existing planes with upgraded cabins, seating, and entertainment systems. By the end of 2026, a majority of the fleet is expected to be either new or fully refurbished.

On the connectivity front, Air India announced a partnership with Hughes Network Systems at the Aircraft Interiors Expo in Hamburg earlier this year to roll out next-generation in-flight connectivity across its widebody fleet. The airline also adopted SITA's OptiFlight technology to optimise fuel efficiency and cut emissions.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the millions of Indians living abroad who rely on Air India for long-haul connections to home, the digital improvements translate into tangible gains: faster booking, real-time disruption handling through AI.g, a revamped loyalty programme in Maharaja Club — which won Program of the Year at the Freddie Awards 2026 — and the promise of broadband-quality in-flight Wi-Fi on international routes.

"Technology will continue to be a key differentiator powering Air India's aspiration to become a world-class global airline."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO and Managing Director, Air India

What's Next

Air India's digital roadmap extends into agentic AI — systems capable of understanding complex contexts and executing tasks autonomously. The airline is building agentic coding capabilities to develop internal software at lower cost and is working with departments to identify AI-driven cost reductions.

The recognition places Air India alongside previous digital-category recipients United Airlines and Ryanair. For a carrier that was widely seen as a turnaround project just four years ago, the award marks a notable validation of its Vihaan.AI transformation strategy — and a signal that the Tata Group's bet on technology-first rebuilding is paying off.
